judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short procedural rule with a ten-day response window and three permitted responses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Calling the decision 'final and binding on the parties but subject to mediation and arbitration' is internally in tension about what finality means.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration of the final accounting 'without a further decision of the Architect', so the Architect's decisional monopoly is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional preclusion depending on the Architect's decision reciting two specific statements; workable but conditional on the Architect's own drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 imposes its own 30-day arbitration deadline running from receipt of the final Certificate, a parallel and differently triggered rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive and short, partly garbled in transcription.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 16 states no bond requirement, so the surety is hypothetical here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short saving provision preserving statutory lien deadlines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) requires lien waivers and Addendum 12.2.2 keys final payment to a lien-free title endorsement, so lien rights are addressed in several places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Heavily garbled in transcription; the underlying mediation mechanics (AAA rules, 60-day stay) are standard but hard to read as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.5.3 and 4.6.1's requirement that mediation precede arbitration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Equal sharing of fees and a default venue at the Project location; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing venue or cost-allocation provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scope clause carves out 'Claims relating to aesthetic effect' and claims waived under other subparagraphs, and the transcription of those exceptions is fragmentary, leaving the arbitration scope uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 provides direct arbitration without an Architect decision, and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves aesthetic control to the Owner, both of which bear on the carve-outs here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the rules and filing requirements specifically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.6.1 and 4.6.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time after the Claim has arisen' sits against fixed cross-referenced deadlines and a statute-of-limitations backstop, mixing three different measures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4's 30-day rule adds a fourth limitation period for a particular class of dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantially involved in a common question of fact or law' and 'whose interest or responsibility is insubstantial' are elastic joinder tests within an otherwise detailed provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses joinder or consolidation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence enforcement provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Paragraph 4.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition with an express exclusion of separate contractors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 10 and Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definitional provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing definition appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule — failure to reply promptly 'shall constitute notice of no reasonable objection' — is definite though 'promptly' is unmeasured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1 sets a materially different regime in which the Contractor obtains bids and the Owner determines which bids are accepted, and Addendum 6.5 requires at least two bids, so subcontractor selection is governed three ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short reciprocal rules turning on 'reasonable and timely objection'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1's final sentence states the Contractor's side of the same rule, and Agreement 10.2 gives the Owner power to require another bid, which this paragraph does not contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably capable of performing' and 'acted promptly and responsively' are judgment standards controlling entitlement to an increase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.2 provides a different remedy for the same situation — a Change Order adjusting the Guaranteed Maximum Price by the bid differential — so two provisions price Owner-forced substitutions differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2.2 and Agreement 10.1's reasonable-objection rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A contingent assignment with three stated conditions; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 imposes a duty to execute assignments as a condition of receiving termination payments, which overlaps with this automatic assignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Equitably adjusted' with a stated suspension threshold; the adjustment measure is open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.4 handles suspension adjustments with its own mapping of 'profit' to the Contractor's Fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reservation of rights with a claim route cross-referenced to 4.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2 and the Claims provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional convention for multi-contract projects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No separate contracts are identified in this instrument, so the provision is dormant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Deemed necessary after a joint review and mutual agreement' conditions schedule revisions on agreement without a fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 create their own schedule-revision regime that becomes part of the Contract Documents, so schedule authority is stated twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including, without excluding others' is an open phrase but the deeming rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1.1 and 6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable opportunity' is soft but the duty is narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1.3 and 3.13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Failure to report is deemed an acknowledgment of fitness 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable', an elastic saving clause on a strict deeming rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 3.2.1's study-and-compare duty and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Improperly timed activities' and 'damage to the Work' are undefined but the reciprocal allocation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.3.10's consequential damages waiver limits what can be recovered under this paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wrongfully caused' is undefined and does more work than it appears to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers consistently to 10.2.5 and to the insurance provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single cross-referencing sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Gives the Architect power to 'allocate the cost among those responsible' without a standard for allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.3 makes debris removal a reimbursable cost, which interacts with but does not contradict this allocation power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enumeration of the three change instruments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 confines changes to Change Orders except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, omitting the minor-change route this paragraph preserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise three-element definition requiring signature by Owner, Contractor and Architect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 makes the Change Order the only route to a price or time change, and Addendum 6.5 contemplates Change Orders being 'issued' as prices are refined, so whether an unsigned or informal adjustment counts is contestable across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragment cross-referring to the listed methods; little content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.1 adopts the same list of methods, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the directive and its unilateral character; the transcription is broken but the substance is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 preserves Paragraph 7.3, so directives remain available notwithstanding the change-order-only rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Method .3 — 'cost to be determined in a manner agreed upon by the parties and a mutually acceptable fixed or percentage fee' — depends on future agreement, and .1 requires 'sufficient substantiating data'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.2 and 6.3 redefine 'cost' and 'fee' for these very provisions by reference to Article 7 and the Contractor's Fee, so the methods must be read through the Agreement's overlay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short duty to proceed and advise; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.3's continuing-performance rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Garbled in transcription, but the effect — a signed directive becomes a Change Order — is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports rather than conflicts with 7.1.3.1's change-order-only rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual net cost as confirmed by the Architect' and the netting rule for combined additions and credits are specific but fact-laden.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.3 maps 'overhead and profit' to the Contractor's Fee, which is a fixed sum here, complicating the netting exercise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Amounts not in dispute' and the Architect's 'interim determination' are workable but leave the disputed portion unresolved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.7.1 expressly incorporates this paragraph into the progress payment calculation, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short recording requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.2.1 and Supplementary Condition 7.2.3's final-settlement rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor changes ... not involving adjustment in the Contract Sum or extension of the Contract Time and not inconsistent with the intent of the Contract Documents' is a boundary that parties frequently contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits changes only by Change Order 'except as permitted in Paragraph 7.3 and Paragraph 9.7.1' — omitting 7.4 — while Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(c) requires Owner and Architect approval of minor field changes, so three provisions govern minor changes inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition with an 'unless otherwise provided' opener; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.3's day-count is garbled and the Addendum substitutes a fixed date, so the Contract Time's content comes from provisions that do not fit together neatly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence pointing to the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1 states an 'approximate' date and Addendum 4.1 makes it 'pending approval of permits', so the date this definition assumes to be 'established' is not firmly established.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition tied to the Architect's certification under 9.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Addendum's bonus provision keyed to Substantial Completion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple default definition of 'day'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement 4.3's use of calendar days and Addendum 12.2.2's 'business days'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Time limits ... are of the essence' is a strong legal characterisation applied wholesale to every time limit in the documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against an approximate commencement date in 4.1, a Contract Time whose day-count is garbled, and an Addendum bonus with no matching liquidated damages provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conditional, though the notice rule ('not less than five days or other agreed period') applies only when commencement is not otherwise established.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1 leaves blank the Owner's time to file mortgages and mechanic's lien notices, and Article 16 states no insurance requirements, so both triggers this paragraph relies on are unspecified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceed expeditiously with adequate forces' is a classic unmeasured performance standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2's skilled-staff obligation and Supplementary Condition 3.10.4's schedule monitoring point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After a list of specific delay causes it adds 'other causes beyond the Contractor's control' and 'other causes which the Architect determines may justify delay' — two successive open-ended catch-alls.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4 bars separate increases for concurrent or interrelated causes and 7.1.3.1 requires a Change Order for any time change, both of which cut into this extension right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.7 and Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract Sum is stated in the Agreement' and is 'the total amount payable' — a definition that assumes a stated figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement states the Contract Sum only as Cost of the Work plus Fee and leaves the Guaranteed Maximum Price as 'N/A', so no total amount payable is in fact stated anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such data substantiating the Contractor's right to payment as the Owner or Architect may require' is a catch-all after specific examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.2-12.1.4 and Addendum 12.1.4 set their own application timing and substantiation lists, so three provisions govern the same submission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short permissive rule cross-referenced to 7.3.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.7.1 incorporates the same mechanism consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Procedures satisfactory to the Owner to establish the Owner's title' is a subjective condition on payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2 address off-site storage on similar terms, so the scheme is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the best of the Contractor's knowledge, information and belief' qualifies an otherwise absolute title warranty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) requires lien waivers over $2,500 and Addendum 12.2.2 requires a lien-free title endorsement, which are stronger requirements built on this warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite seven-day certification deadline with two alternatives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 expressly states that its time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1', so the two provisions are in acknowledged competition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long, but each representation is expressly qualified and the four disclaimers are itemised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.9 makes the same disclaimers in near-identical terms, an overlap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably necessary to protect the Owner', 'in the Architect's opinion' and 'reasonable evidence' govern an enumerated list of seven grounds, several of which (notably .5, completion for the unpaid balance) are themselves evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ground .5 measures the unpaid balance against 'the Contract Sum', which in this cost-plus contract has no fixed figure because the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A', and ground .6 refers to liquidated damages that were never inserted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single restorative sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.5.1.
